title: Queens Placement
statement:
Place n queens on an n-by-n chessboard so that no two attack each other, and list every such arrangement.

Contract
- `n` is at least 1; throw `IllegalArgumentException` for anything smaller. Queens attack along rows, columns and both diagonals.
- A board is a list of `n` strings of length `n`, one per row, using `'Q'` for a queen and `'.'` for an empty square.
- Return every distinct board exactly once. The order of the boards is up to you.
- If no arrangement exists, return an empty list.

Examples
- `solveQueens(4)` returns two boards: `[".Q..", "...Q", "Q...", "..Q."]` and `["..Q.", "Q...", "...Q", ".Q.."]` in any order.
- `solveQueens(1)` returns `[["Q"]]`.
- `solveQueens(3)` returns an empty list.
hints: Each row must hold exactly one queen, so decide the queens one row at a time.
Try each column in the current row, skipping squares attacked by earlier rows. Track used columns and both diagonal directions in constant-time lookups, and undo the choice after exploring it.

Row minus column identifies one diagonal and row plus column identifies the other. Intended complexity: the general search is exponential, roughly O(n!) time with O(n) working space per branch plus the output. The scaling probe repeatedly solves a fixed 6-by-6 board and keeps the results, so it grows linearly in the number of repeats (n) in both time and space.
inputSyntax: Input: the board size n, for example: 6
